harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a MariaDB Galera cluster from scratch on node1/node2/node3 (Ubuntu 16.04 i386), then added node4 as a fourth member carrying existing application data and accepting writes. Ubuntu's native mariadb-server-10.0 package on this i386 image lacks wsrep/Galera support (confirmed: "unknown variable 'wsrep_on'"), so switched to the official MariaDB 10.1 i386 repo, which does include full wsrep support (104 wsrep options found via mysqld --help --verbose). node1 was bootstrapped as the founding cluster member with an appdb.orders table and seed rows; node2 and node3 joined via automatic rsync SST and replicated the existing data; node4 was installed identically, its config fixed to load from the correct conf.d path (its fresh install lacked the mariadb.conf.d include used by the others), and joined the running cluster, receiving the same data via SST. Cross-node writes from node3 and node4 confirmed multi-master replication to all peers. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline on each node, restarted each of the 4 nodes one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (never more than one down at once, quorum preserved throughout since only 1 of 4 was ever offline), confirmed each node's boot_id changed post-restart, and verified mysql auto-started (SysV rc2.d symlinks) with wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, wsrep_cluster_size=4, and all application data intact. Final end-to-end write/read check across nodes confirms the 4-member cluster is healthy and consistent.
actions_performed: Investigated existing cluster state on all 4 nodes (none had MariaDB installed)
Installed mariadb-server-10.0 + galera-3 on node1/2/3 from Ubuntu repos; discovered wsrep support absent on this i386 build
Added official MariaDB 10.1 i386 xenial repo, purged 10.0 packages, reinstalled mariadb-server-10.1 + galera-3 on node1/2/3
Fixed missing /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d directory blocking postinst mysql_install_db
Wrote wsrep/Galera config (60-galera.cnf) to node1/2/3 with gcomm addresses
Bootstrapped node1 as founding cluster member (wsrep-new-cluster)
Created appdb.orders table with seed data on node1 before adding peers
Started node2 and node3; verified automatic SST sync of existing data and cluster_size growth to 2 then 3
Verified multi-master replication (write on node3 visible on node1)
Installed mariadb-server-10.1 + galera-3 fresh on node4 from the same MariaDB repo
Diagnosed and fixed node4's config include-path mismatch (my.cnf only included /etc/mysql/conf.d, not mariadb.conf.d) so wsrep options were silently ignored
Updated node1/2/3 gcomm address lists to include node4 for future restarts
Started node4; confirmed SST join, cluster_size=4, Synced/Primary, and all pre-existing data present
Verified write from node4 propagates to node1/2/3
Enabled SysV rc-boot autostart verification (rc2.d symlinks) on all nodes

Executed mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline, restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed mysql active with wsrep Synced/Primary/cluster_size=4 and data intact after each restart
Ran final cross-node write/read consistency check post all-restarts

evidence.summary: node4 joined with wsrep_cluster_size=4, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, and SELECT on appdb.orders returned all pre-existing rows from node1/2/3

evidence.summary: Fresh write on node1 after all restarts was immediately visible on node4, confirming end-to-end replication health across the restarted 4-node cluster
